title: Lamarr — IHH content reconciliation
header: Private editorial working note, 17 October 2026. **REQUIRES HUMAN SIGN-OFF.** This is not approved visitor copy. No changes to `inductees/lamarr/copy.md` are authorized by this note.

IHH starting page: [hedy-lamarr](https://immigranthallofhonor.org/inductees/inductee-hedy-lamarr/), retrieved during this review. Line references identify the retrieved text view, not a stable page anchor. Facts are inventoried below in IHH’s order. Compound rows retain all their components; NOT VERIFIED applies to each component unless a narrower status is explicitly stated.
Independent source read: [National Inventors Hall of Fame](https://www.invent.org/inductees/hedy-lamarr). A page being available does not verify every claim on IHH.

NIHF: National Inventors Hall of Fame, “Hedy Lamarr”

evidence: Actress Hedy Lamarr was best known for her work in Hollywood during its Golden Age
L10.note: Every part of the IHH claim appears in the quoted text from National Inventors Hall of Fame.

L11.claim: Birth Name: Hedwig Eva Maria Kiesler
evidence: Also known as: Hedwig Eva Maria Kiesler
L11.note: Every part of the IHH claim appears in the quoted text from Encyclopædia Britannica.

L12.note: Note: Britannica gives the birth year as “1913/14”; the National Inventors Hall of Fame gives 1914.

evidence: died January 19, 2000, near Orlando, Florida, U.S.
L13.note: Date confirmed. Britannica says “near Orlando”; Casselberry (a suburb of Orlando) is not named in the retrieved text.

L15.claim: Education: Max Reinhardt’s Berlin Dramatic School, 1929
evidence: At age 16 she enrolled in Max Reinhardt’s Berlin-based dramatic school
L15.note: The school is confirmed. Britannica gives her age (16), not a year. Given the 1913/14 birth-year uncertainty, 1929 cannot be confirmed.

evidence: Actress Hedy Lamarr was best known for her work in Hollywood during its Golden Age
Lamarr also worked with Hollywood composer George Antheil to invent a frequency hopping technique
L16.note: Every part of the IHH claim appears in the quoted text from National Inventors Hall of Fame.

evidence: Lamarr became a U.S. citizen in 1953.
L17.note: Every part of the IHH claim appears in the quoted text from Encyclopædia Britannica.

evidence: Lamarr also worked with Hollywood composer George Antheil to invent a frequency hopping technique
L29.note: Co-invention with George Antheil is confirmed. The 1941 date (the patent application) is not in this source; the patent itself, already in our profile’s manifest, records the filing date.

evidence: When the patent was issued in 1942, it listed her maiden and married name at the time, Hedy Kiesler Markey.

L31.note: No filmography count was checked. Britannica names individual films but gives no total.

L38.claim: Star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame (1960)
evidence: Category Motion Pictures Address 6247 Hollywood Blvd. Ceremony date 02/08/1960
L38.note: Every part of the IHH claim appears in the quoted text from Hollywood Walk of Fame.

L39.claim: Won the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) Pioneer Award (1997)
evidence: it was acknowledged by the Electronic Frontier Foundation in 1997 as an important development in wireless communications
L39.note: The National Inventors Hall of Fame records the 1997 EFF recognition; EFF’s own Pioneer Award list was not retrieved.

L40.claim: First woman to win the Invention Convention’s Bulbie Gnass Spirit of Achievement Award (1997)
L40.note: No record of the 1997 Invention Convention “Bulbie” award was retrieved.

L41.claim: Inducted into the National Inventors Hall of Fame (2014)
evidence: Frequency Hopping Communication System U.S. Patent No. 2,292,387 Inducted in 2014
L41.note: Every part of the IHH claim appears in the quoted text from National Inventors Hall of Fame.
